name: Ningil
catalog_quote: 5.1 Stress Stress tends to occur on the first and every alternate syllable. ... /paligi/ ['pal9'gi] ... /tapapi/ ['daba'bi] ... There are a few two syllable words where the stress seems to be on the second syllable. ... When there is a prefix added, stress may be on the second syllable. /pewegAf/ [po'wegAr] 'tame' (possessive prefix 'p©')

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding passage (the domain quotation) is verbatim on p.65 of the held Manning & Saggers 1977, and the transcribed examples directly show 101 (3-syll) and 1010 (4-syll), matching the coded alternating stress from the left (initial stress plus alternating rhythm). The source is the sole descriptive phonology of Ningil per Glottolog 5.1, so the best available description is. It is nonetheless a short, self-described 'tentative' SIL statement: the rule is hedged ('tends to'), a handful of disyllables show second-syllable stress, prefixed forms shift stress to the stem-initial (second) syllable, primary vs secondary stress is not distinguished, and 5+-syllable patterns are projected rather than exemplified (as the record's own correction note already says). Nothing suggests the classification is wrong, and no better source exists to change it, so status 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced'. Action: the
